access.edition_or_version: First edition, Indian Thought Publications, Madras, 1943 (150 pp.); enlarged 1982 Viking edition

mechanics.premise: Connected stories of the imagined South Indian town Malgudi and its merchants, schoolboys, magicians, and clerks; no overarching plot - the town itself is the continuity.
mechanics.point_of_view: Third-person limited, rotating across townspeople, with a lightly ironic narrator.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Close enough to feel each character's small stakes, held back by the narrator's gentle irony so warmth never tips into mawkishness.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Plain lucid prose; comic timing; concrete local detail (names, trades, landmarks); understated pathos; seasonal and festival rhythm.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Each story: ordinary situation - small complication - humane resolution or wry deflation; the collection's arc is accretive familiarity rather than climax.
mechanics.dialogue: Idiom-inflected English carrying local speech rhythms; dialogue does much of the characterization work.
mechanics.conventions: Regional short-story tradition with the town as organizing principle.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Builds a nostalgic object (the town) that never existed, and lets affection grow from observation rather than declaration - restorative impulse without restorative rhetoric.
mechanics.critical_reception: Enduring reputation as a classic of Indian English fiction; a standard school text in India.
mechanics.audience_reception: Readers describe rereading the stories as a return to a place they know (Guardian rereading essay, 2011); the stories were adapted for Indian television in the 1980s.
